questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: When I choose to go on exchange, I wanted to go to Australia because my parents have lived in Australia. I then looked into the different schools, and wanted a good school with interesting classes in a fun town with many opportunities. And then I found University of Sydney which matched all my criteria.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Exchange was the best experience, and I am so glad I took the chance and went on exchange.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think University of Sydney was really good at giving information before and upon arrival. They had introduction days and an introduction meeting where they informed us of all the practical information but also all the good to know or fun to know.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a counselor that send us e-mails guiding us through the first couple of weeks. My counselor was really helpfull, I has to switch classes so I had to meet up with her. She was good at guiding me through my different choices and helped me with my timetabel/schedule.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The only problem, was that they send too many mails - but that is better than too few.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through a group on facebook for Danes on exchange in Sydney. One of the other students wrote she was going to live in a share house and there was still rooms available. So I was lucky it was very easy for me. But I have heard other people struggle finding housing off campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I loved living off campus, I lived by the beach. It was difinetly less expensive than the housing on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think the housing available on campus is very expensive and not that good.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Easy to register, but hard to find out if the classes matched with your schedule.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We choose 10 courses and then my host institution got approval from the teachers to all the courses I was able to take. Then I online choose the 4 courses I wanted to be enrolled in. I later switched a class before arrival, and to do so I just had to write and email to my counselor and she was able to change my enrollment.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
Our counselor was able to help us with any questions we had. 
Also the homepage of University of Sydney was helpful with details of the different courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I think the whole process was stressfull, a lot of things to take into account and think about all the time.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take good time to choose the right classes for you. Don't choose 4 classes that seem very hard, find a good mix. If you regret or doubt a class don't hesitate to ask your counselor for advice. Also don't stress too hard over the classes, most students drop and switch class within the first two weeks of school.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The classes were very interesting and they had a many different choices, which I really liked.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I mostly had courses for students on their 3rd year of their bachelors.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Pretty much the same, we had lectures, practical classes and workshops. 
So very much like my classes at University of Sydney

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Biochemistry of Human disease 
Human neuroscience in Health and disease 
Learning in outdoor education 
Infectious diseases

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
You have to take learning in outdoor education. It is a class only for exchange students, where you explore the Australian nature while you get to know people from all over the world. 

My other classes I also really enjoyed, they were hard so took a lot of my time. I would probably recommend not taking that hard classes together. I should have switched one of them out with an easier course,

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Visa cost 3500, which is a lot. 
Then alcohol is expensive in Australia, going out in general is very expensive. 
Traveling in Australia is also expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I was lucky all my books were online, but books are expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They don't really have any clubs I wanted to join. They don't have sports teams at the school you can join, so that was a little sad.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have different clubs like different language clubs, cultural food clubs and adventure clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend using hostels when traveling and going on the trips arranged by the school for exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I think Melbourne is really cool to visit. 
Western Australia is a must in my mind. It was really cool, you have the red sand and the beautiful blue ocean. Just very pretty and so different. 
In my mind the east cost is overrated. I would do a weekend trip to Byron bay, magnetic island and whitsundays. The rest of the east coast I would skip. 
Also great ocean road is very beautiful, and if you like nature and hikes this is the perfect place.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Very easy, Sydney is very much like Copenhagen. 
The atmosphere is very casual.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and not afraid to just ask them a question. Australians are very kind, helpfull people, so honestly should not be a problem if you just talk to them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Their school system is very different from ours. That was a little hard figuring out in the beginning. 
Usually they don't take a master, since they are done after the 4th year of their bachelors - this makes the courses in science at least a little bit more carrer orientated. 
Also they can take majors and minors.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The chilled atmosphere. 
You have a large city and then the beach right next to it - which is really amazing.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Come with an open mind 
2. Throw yourself out there and try things you normally would not. 
3. Enjoy it, it is over before you know it

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Buy your sim-card at the airport that is less expensive.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
All the friendships and traveling. 
Australia is beautiful and has so much to offer.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Being away from your support system at home. 
All people went through some kind of home-sickness, and it is so normal. Talk to your new friends they probably know the feeling and want to help you the best they can.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy ! I wish it was me going on exchange again.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
